{"body":"CUDA `findPeakAndInterpolateKernel` evaluates the five selected float CCF samples and the parabola vertex in float. On a large DC pedestal, `vp + vn - 2*maxval` loses curvature through cancellation. CPU evaluates the same stored float samples in double.

Captured witness (#250/#256): m=36366.4296875, vp=36365.69140625, vn=36366.359375, scale=4. CPU gives -1.6521739130434783 px; CUDA gives -1.6442307233810425 px on identical samples. Host replay found effects up to 0.135252 px. The kernel serves global and local alignment.

Fix scope: promote only the five samples and fit arithmetic to double; preserve integer peak selection, the existing 1e-15 guard semantics and scale application. Add a native CUDA same-map regression with a float-denominator mutant, flat/near-guard and boundary cases. Run full Release CPU/CUDA/CUDA+nvCOMP suites on 4GPUs and retain evidence. Intentional output differences correct the demonstrated CUDA arithmetic defect; this alone does not establish S1 closure or scientific equivalence.

Related: #238, #232, #250, #256. Production change is independent of #254; combined S1 attribution will be a separate evidence-only PR. No merge by the implementation agent.
","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOUnH-pc8AAAABd8iioQ","author":{"login":"KingAlejandro"},"authorAssociation":"OWNER","body":"## Independent guidance for the active peak-fit experiment

Promoting the selected samples is a well-motivated, narrowly scoped experiment. The objective should be accurate evaluation of the parabola **on the stored samples**, not bitwise replication of the complete CPU pipeline. Please keep this issue independent of #254 and put combined attribution in an evidence-only follow-up.

### Corrections to the rationale

- The **0.13525164 px** maximum in #250/#256 is already in the candidate's **image/patch-pixel units after the CCF scale**, with the GPU float scale held fixed. It is not 0.135 CCF-grid pixels to be scaled again.
- The approximately 0.045 px first-global-iteration difference in the five S1.3 cases is an observation, not an upper bound on final accumulated trajectories across the later census. Reference-frame subtraction, repeated updates, changed maps and stopping decisions can amplify smaller differences. Comparing it directly with a 0.30 px census maximum does not establish a missing error budget or prove this particular cause.
- This is a demonstrated avoidable arithmetic contribution, but not the only possible remaining source. Valid FFT/map differences, ambiguous peaks, reference-frame anchoring, convergence and acceptance sensitivity remain. The equal-trajectory controls establish where sensitivity enters for the sampled movies, not which scalar operation explains every remaining case.

### Implementation/test contract

1. Call the **actual production peak kernel** with identical saved CCF bytes and compare to an independent promoted/high-precision same-sample oracle. Keep integer winner/tie order unchanged; test global, batched local and retry entry points. Do not duplicate a corrected expression in a separate test-only kernel and call that production coverage.
2. Specify promotion, threshold, scale and output casts separately. The kernel currently accepts float scales and writes float candidates (see [calls and host feedback at 8b55d5da](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/8b55d5da/src/acc/cuda/cuda_alignpatch.cu#L636-L680)); a double vertex alone does **not** guarantee exact CPU candidates or trajectories. Preserve the chosen scale convention for the first causal comparison, and document whether the vertex is rounded before or after multiplication.
3. “Preserve guard semantics” must mean retaining a defined threshold/fallback rule, not preserving every old branch result. I independently checked the float32 witness `m=vp=1`, `vn=nextafterf(1,0)`: old denominator is exactly 0; promoted denominator is `-2^-24`, giving a +0.5 CCF-pixel correction. That branch change is a consequence of fixing the arithmetic. Test it explicitly rather than forcing the broken zero result. Include flat maps, unique one-ULP peaks, ties, unbracketed search-edge neighbours, near-threshold values, non-finite inputs and the actual Release compiler/FTZ/contraction settings. Keep any new peak-validity policy separate.
4. Retain baseline / Hermitian-only / peak-only / both builds from one pinned base. On the main diagnostic movies, additionally distinguish global-only from local-only promotion. Log first changed samples, winners, candidates, reference-frame subtraction, per-iteration RMSD and stopping, final global trajectories, accepted patch sets, full-precision model coefficients, and DW/non-DW image metrics. Do not limit evaluation to the previously positive configurations.
5. Selective FP64 is plausibly inexpensive, but **cost is unmeasured**, not automatically negligible. Report kernel and whole-movie overhead on the intended hardware without introducing per-frame debug synchronisation in the production path.

No new native CUDA run is claimed by this comment. The small guard witness above is a host IEEE-float replay. A lower CPU-relative RMSE would be useful evidence, not proof of better recovered motion; retain known-truth and S1.4 scientific checks.","createdAt":"2026-10-21T00:04:52Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"isMinimized":false,"minimizedReason":"","reactionGroups":[],"url":"https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/issues/257#issuecomment-6304604833","viewerDidAuthor":true}],"title":"CUDA subpixel peak fit loses precision in float denominator"}
